guides.title: Give a farmer a contract
guides.blurb: Assign a contract from a template, with its dates, size and product.

steps.title: Contract Management
steps.text: Click Contract Management.

steps.title: Manage Contracts
steps.text: Click Manage Contracts.

steps.title: Assign Contract
steps.text: Click Assign Contract.

steps.title: 1. Farmer and template
steps.text: Choose the farmer and the contract template.

steps.title: 2. Dates
steps.text: From and to, or tick permanent.

steps.title: 3. Size and product
steps.text: The contract size and the tobacco type.

steps.title: 4. Field location
steps.text: Where the field is, if you have it.

steps.title: Assign Contract
steps.text: Creates the contract. It then follows your approval workflow (or is approved straight away if none applies).

guides.title: Import locations
guides.blurb: Load your regions, areas and clubs from an Excel or CSV file, then read what was added and what was skipped.

steps.title: Locations Master
steps.text: Click Locations Master.

steps.title: 1. Download the template
steps.text:
Download Template gives you an Excel file with one column per Hierarchy Level, from the top down (e.g. Region, Area, Club). Tobacco Type and Warehouse columns are added when you have them, then your Location Fields.
Fill in one row per club and repeat the parent names on every row. Leave no gaps: a name can't sit to the right of an empty cell.

steps.title: Changing what is already there?
steps.text: Export Locations downloads every location with the same columns as the template. Edit that file and import it back.

steps.title: Import History
steps.text: Lists recent imports with who ran them and how many locations were added, changed or removed. Only the latest import can be undone.

steps.title: 2. Import Areas
steps.text:
Click Import Areas and choose your filled-in file (.xlsx, .xls or .csv). The headings must match your Hierarchy Levels.
The guide carries on when the import options appear.
steps.hint: Click Import Areas and choose your file

steps.title: 3. Add & update (the safe choice)
steps.text: Adds new locations and fills in values. Nothing is renamed, moved or cleared, and a blank cell never removes a value. A location whose full path already exists is not added again.

steps.title: The other two options
steps.text:
Overwrite: your locations become exactly this file. Any location not in the file is removed (or switched off if farmers, contracts or users are on it).
Move under new parents: moves existing locations, with everything under them, to the parent named in the file.
Use these only when you mean it. You can undo afterwards.

steps.title: 4. Import and read the results
steps.text:
Pick an option, then click Import. The Import Results window shows New areas created, Already existed (skipped, never duplicated) and Rows read.
Rows that were skipped are listed in red with the reason (for example an empty cell to the left of a name). Fix them and import the same file again; rows that already went in are skipped.
Imported areas have no map pin yet. Wrong file? Click Undo this import.

guides.title: Import farmers
guides.blurb: Load or update many farmers from Excel with the import wizard: say what you want to do, choose the file, match the columns, check, then import.

steps.title: Farmers Master
steps.text: Click Farmers Master.

steps.title: Data Tools
steps.text: Click Data Tools.

steps.title: 1. Get the template
steps.text:
Download Blank Template: First Name, Last Name, Contract Number, ID Number, Passport Number, Phone Number, Physical Address, one drop-down column per hierarchy level, then your own profile fields.
One row per farmer. Photos and documents can't be imported.

steps.title: Import History
steps.text: View Import History lists every import with its new and updated farmers. Rollback removes the new farmers of that import and puts the updated ones back as they were (farmers changed by hand since are left alone). It fails once a new farmer has a contract.

steps.title: 2. Import Excel Data
steps.text: Click Import Excel Data. The import wizard opens - nothing is saved until its last step.

steps.title: 1. What do you want to do?
steps.text:
Add new farmers and update existing ones: the usual choice - nobody is removed.
Update existing farmers only: for a file from Export Farmer Data that you changed - nobody is added.
Replace the whole farmer list: the file is your complete list; farmers not in it move to Deactivated Profiles (nothing is deleted).
Choose one, then click Next.

steps.title: 2. Choose your file
steps.text: Click here (or drop the file on it) and choose your Excel file. When the file has several sheets, pick the one with the farmers. Say whether row 1 holds the column names, then click Next.

steps.title: 3. Match the columns
steps.text: Each column of your file, with example values, and the field it goes into. They are guessed from the column names - and matched the way you did it last time. Set a column to Ignore to leave it out. The ticks above show what is still needed (for example First Name). Then click Check the file.

steps.title: 4. Check
steps.text: How many farmers are added, updated (and move club), and which rows are left out with the reason - Download the problem rows to fix them. A club that is not on the system is asked about first (create it?). For Replace, you see who would be deactivated. Blank cells keep what is saved. Nothing is saved yet.

steps.title: 5. Import now
steps.text: A plain summary of what happens. Click Import now: everything is saved as one import (Replace asks you to type the number of farmers to deactivate first). Then choose Keep the import or Roll back now.

guides.title: Import warehouses & stock items
guides.blurb: Load your warehouses, then your stock catalogue with prices, from Excel.

steps.title: Distribution Master
steps.text: Click Distribution Master.

steps.title: Warehouses
steps.text: Click Warehouses.

steps.title: Data Tools
steps.text: Click Data Tools.

steps.title: 1. Warehouses
steps.text:
Blank Import Template has two columns: Warehouse Name (required) and Linked Area (optional, typed as it appears in Locations).
After this guide, click Import Excel Data and pick the file. A preview marks each row NEW, UPDATE (same name, new area), NO CHANGE or REJECTED (no name, name repeated, area not found). Click Import to save. Rejected rows are skipped.

steps.title: 2. Stock Items
steps.text: Now the stock catalogue. Click Stock Items.

steps.title: Data Tools
steps.text: Click Data Tools. It has Blank Import Template (Item Code, Item Name, Category, Unit of Measure, Cost Price, Contractor Price, Description, Status) and View Import History.

steps.title: Import Excel Data
steps.text: Click Import Excel Data.

steps.title: 3. Choose your file
steps.text:
Click the file box and choose your Excel file (.xlsx or .xls). Rows to ignore at top stays on 1 for the template, which skips the heading row.
The guide carries on when the columns appear.
steps.hint: Click the file box and choose your file

steps.title: 4. Match the columns
steps.text:
Check each column's match. Item Code and Item Name are required. Tobacco Type and Cat 1-4 Qty per ha columns fill that tobacco type's recipe.
Then click Preview Staging Area. Nothing is saved yet.

steps.title: 5. Check, then commit
steps.text:
Rows show NEW, UPDATE (the Item Code already exists) or REJECTED (no code or name, or a code repeated in the file). Leave the boxes ticked to create new units and categories, or those rows fail.
Click Commit Import (or Import Valid Rows Only). View Import History can roll back a batch's new items. Updates stay.

guides.title: Import manager assignments
guides.blurb: Give many managers their areas at once from an Excel file.

steps.title: Contractors Hierarchy
steps.text: Click Contractors Hierarchy.

steps.title: Manager Assignments
steps.text: Click Manager Assignments.

steps.title: Data Tools
steps.text: Click Data Tools.

steps.title: 1. Get the template
steps.text:
Download Blank Template: a Username column plus one column per hierarchy level, all with drop-downs.
One row per manager and area. Repeat a username to give them several areas. Fill in only the level they manage (e.g. just the Club). The levels above it are worked out.

steps.title: 2. Bulk Upload Assignments
steps.text:
Click Bulk Upload Assignments and choose your filled-in file (.xlsx or .xls).
The guide carries on when the preview appears.
steps.hint: Click Bulk Upload Assignments and choose your file

steps.title: 3. Check the preview
steps.text:
The top line says how many pairings are ready. Problem rows come first: red SKIPPED rows (username or area not found) and amber FLAGGED rows (the name fits more than one location, so add the level above or the unique number).
These rows are left out and everything else can still be applied. Print the problem rows as a PDF to fix them.

steps.title: Discard
steps.text: Clears the preview. Nothing has been saved yet, so nothing changes.

steps.title: 4. Apply Assignments
steps.text:
Saves the pairings. Each manager then receives approvals, escalations and notifications for those areas and sees only the farmers in them. Nothing they already hold is removed.
The next screen lets you roll it back if it came out wrong.

guides.title: Add locations & the hierarchy
guides.blurb: Add your hierarchy levels, a location, and a manager over it.

steps.title: Farmers Hierarchy
steps.text: First your levels, then your locations, then the managers. Click Farmers Hierarchy.

steps.title: Hierarchy Levels
steps.text: Levels are your structure from the top down, for example REGION, then AREA, then CLUB. Click Hierarchy Levels.

steps.title: Add Level
steps.text: Click Add Level.

steps.title: Name it and save
steps.text: Type the Level Name, e.g. REGION. If you already have levels, pick its Position: Top, between two levels, or Bottom. Click Save Level; it is saved straight away. Start with the top level, then use Add Level again for each level under it.
steps.hint: Fill in, then click Save Level

steps.title: Locations Master
steps.text: Now the locations. Click Locations Master.

steps.title: Add Area
steps.text: Click Add Area to add one location by hand. For many at once, use Download Template and then Import Areas.

steps.title: Name, parent and level
steps.text: Area Name. Parent Area: the location it sits under (leave blank for a top location). Hierarchy Level: its level, e.g. CLUB. Area Radius: the size of its circle on the map. For a club, also pick its Tobacco Type.

steps.title: Map and Save Area
steps.text: Fill in the form and drag the pin on the map to the right spot. The circle must fit inside its parent's circle, or it won't save: move the pin or make the radius smaller. Click Save Area.
steps.hint: Fill in, then click Save Area

steps.title: Manager Assignments
steps.text: Back on Farmers Hierarchy: put a manager over a location. Click Manager Assignments.

steps.title: Assign managers
steps.text: Managers are assigned from a spreadsheet. Data Tools > Download Blank Template. Fill in one row per manager and location: the Username and the location under each level. Leave the deeper levels blank to give them a whole region. Then Data Tools > Bulk Upload Assignments, check the preview and click Apply Assignments. Contracts from that location then come to that manager's Inbox for approval.

guides.title: Add warehouses, stock items & receive stock
guides.blurb: Create a warehouse and a stock item, receive stock with a GRV, and see it in the inventory.

steps.title: Warehouses
steps.text: This is Distribution Master (sidebar, under Distribution). First a warehouse: click Warehouses.

steps.title: Create Warehouse
steps.text: Click Create Warehouse.

steps.title: Name and area
steps.text: Type the Warehouse Name and choose the Linked Geographic Area. Locations under that area are covered too. Click Save.

steps.title: Stock Items
steps.text: Next, the inputs you hand out. Click Stock Items.

steps.title: Create Item
steps.text: Click Create Item. No units yet? Add them first with Units (UoM).

steps.title: Item details
steps.text: Fill in Item Code / SKU, Item Name and Unit (UoM) (required), plus Category (e.g. Fertilizer), Cost Price and Farmer Price. Tick Requires Batch/Lot Tracking to record batch numbers when stock is received. Click Save Item.
steps.hint: Fill in, then click Save Item

steps.title: Receive Stock (GRV)
steps.text: Now book stock into the warehouse. Click Receive Stock (GRV).

steps.title: Receive New Stock
steps.text: Click Receive New Stock.

steps.title: Items and quantities
steps.text: Type the PO / Ref Number and choose the Destination Warehouse. For each item: Select Bulk Item, type the Quantity (and Batch/Lot No if asked), click Add. Then click Process GRV; the stock is added to that warehouse.
steps.hint: Add the items, then click Process GRV

steps.title: Where it shows
steps.text: Click Live Inventory & Transfers: one tile per warehouse with its stock. Open a warehouse for its totals, each item and every movement. Transfer Stock moves stock between warehouses.

guides.title: Set up a season & tobacco types
guides.blurb: Add a growing season, use its dates for contracts, and add a tobacco type with its recipe.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Click Settings. It opens as a pop-up window.

steps.title: Seasons
steps.text: Under Season & products, click Seasons.

steps.title: Add Season
steps.text: To add a season, click Add Season (after this guide). Only one season can be active: while one is active the button is faded - first deactivate it with the red button on its row (it is kept for the record). In the pop-up type the Season Name, Start Date and End Date, then click Save Season.

steps.title: Use for contracts
steps.text: Switch this on in the active season's row and every new contract, on the web and on the phones, runs from the season's start date to its end date. The date boxes are hidden and running contracts get the season's end date. You are asked to confirm first. With no active season, no contract can be added.

steps.title: History
steps.text: History lists every change: who, when, the old and new values, and how many contracts were updated.

steps.title: Tobacco Types & Recipes
steps.text: Click Tobacco Types & Recipes.

steps.title: Add tobacco type
steps.text: Click Add tobacco type.

steps.title: Code and name
steps.text: Type a short Tobacco Type Code (e.g. VIR), the Tobacco Type Name (e.g. Virginia Flue-Cured) and an optional Description. Click Add tobacco type. Its recipe opens straight after. A club gets its tobacco type in Locations Master.
steps.hint: Fill in, then click Add tobacco type

steps.title: The recipe
steps.text: The recipe is the default list of inputs for this tobacco type. Pick a Stock Item, a Math Rule (a fixed amount, or multiplied by the contract size) and the Base Qty, then click +. Later, the list button on a row (Edit recipe) opens the recipe again and the pencil edits the tobacco type. Each distribution cycle gets a copy of the recipe that can be changed for that cycle.

guides.title: Set up contract approvals
guides.blurb: Who approves a contract, how far up it goes, and the approvers' signatures.

steps.title: Workflow
steps.text: A contract starts at the farmer's own location and goes up, location by location. At each step, the managers over that location approve it in their Inbox (managers are set in Farmers Hierarchy > Manager Assignments). The rules are here: click Workflow.

steps.title: Approval Timers (SLAs)
steps.text: Click Approval Timers (SLAs).

steps.title: One row per level
steps.text: Every workflow is listed at the top - Edit opens this pop-up. These are the rules for Contracts (Distribution has its own). Auto-Escalate (Days) passes the contract up after that many days waiting. Auto-Approve (Days) approves it after that many days (0 = off). Approve On Arrival? approves it at that level straight away. Approve From Mobile App? lets that level's managers approve on the phone.

steps.title: Is Final Level?
steps.text: Tick Is Final Level? on the last level that must approve. Once approved there, the contract is fully approved and goes no higher. With none ticked, it goes up to the top. Value Rule?, if shown, gives clubs that meet a number rule (e.g. hectares) a different final level.

steps.title: Save Rules
steps.text: Make your changes in the table, then click Save Rules.
steps.hint: Make changes, then click Save Rules

steps.title: Path Preview
steps.text: Check who a contract will go to. Click Path Preview.

steps.title: Who approves
steps.text: Choose a location in Select Starting Area to see every step a contract from there goes through and who approves it. A red No Manager Assigned means nobody approves at that step: add a manager in Farmers Hierarchy > Manager Assignments. This is a check only. Someone away? Stand-In Approvers sends their approvals to someone else between two dates.

steps.title: Approvers' signatures
steps.text: Each approver can have a saved signature. Click Settings.

steps.title: Manager Signatures
steps.text: Under Contracts, click Manager Signatures.

steps.title: Add Approver
steps.text: Click Add Approver, pick the user, then Draw the signature, Import image, or choose Later, and click Save. When that person approves a contract, their saved signature is copied onto it for the Approver signature boxes on your contract template. Approvers can also sign for themselves here.

guides.title: Create a contract template
guides.blurb: Import your contract as a PDF, place the farmer details and signature boxes on it, and choose the default contract for the phones.

steps.title: Contract Management
steps.text: Click Contract Management.

steps.title: Contract Templates
steps.text: Click Contract Templates.

steps.title: Your templates
steps.text: Every template with its version. PDF · 5 fields means it is ready; PDF · Not mapped means no boxes are placed yet, so it cannot be used to assign a contract. The pencil opens Map Fields again; the power button deactivates a template (contracts already made keep it).

steps.title: Default contract
steps.text: The star makes this the default contract on the phones: it is pre-selected when a club signs (the field technician can still pick another). Phones get the change at their next Sync.

steps.title: Version history
steps.text: Shows every version. When a template already used by contracts is changed, a new version is made, so signed contracts keep the layout they were signed on.

steps.title: Import Contract PDF
steps.text: Click Import Contract PDF and choose your contract (a PDF). It is kept exactly as it is, and Map Fields opens on it.
steps.hint: Click Import Contract PDF and choose the file

steps.title: Draw a box
steps.text: Drag on the page to draw a box where a value must be printed, e.g. the farmer's name or a signature. Use the arrows on the right to go to the other pages.

steps.title: Choose what goes in the box
steps.text: After you draw a box, Map this area to appears here. Choose the field (farmer details, contract dates and size, the farmer's signature and photo, approver signatures, Chairperson, Secretary, club and witness boxes) and click Assign. Every box is listed under Mapped Fields.

steps.title: Save Field Map
steps.text: Click Save Field Map when all boxes are placed. The template can then be chosen in Assign Contract, and the phones get it at their next Sync. Use the star to make it the default.

guides.title: Add custom fields
guides.blurb: Add your own fields to locations, farmer profiles (including document uploads) and contracts.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Click Settings. It opens as a pop-up window.

steps.title: Location Fields
steps.text: Click Location Fields: extra information kept on each location in Locations Master, e.g. a club's Biometric Number or Hectares.

steps.title: Add a location field
steps.text: Add field opens a pop-up: the Field Name, Data Type (Text or Number), an optional Symbol (e.g. $), the level it Applies To, Mandatory and Unique (no two locations may have the same value). On the list, the pencil edits a field and the red button deactivates it.

steps.title: Profile Fields & Documents
steps.text: Click Profile Fields & Documents: extra fields on every farmer profile.

steps.title: Add a profile field
steps.text: Add field: give it a name and a type - Text, Number, Date, Yes / No or Document Upload (e.g. a tax clearance). Tick Mandatory if it must be filled in. It shows on the farmer profile (Location & Docs tab) and on the phones after their next Sync. The pencil edits it; the red button deactivates it (old values are kept under Deactivated).

steps.title: Profile overview & phone app
steps.text: Choose up to 3 fields to show under the farmer's name on the profile overview and in the phone app's farmer lists. Saved as soon as you choose; phones use it after their next Sync.

steps.title: Contract Fields
steps.text: Click Contract Fields: extra details captured on each contract when it is assigned.

steps.title: Mandatory switch
steps.text: Switch Mandatory on and the field must be filled in, on the web and in the phone app. One click saves it.

steps.title: Add a contract field
steps.text: Click Add field.

steps.title: Name, type and Mandatory
steps.text: Type the Attribute Name, choose the Data Type (Text, Number or Date), tick Mandatory if needed, then click Add field. It is asked when a contract is assigned, and on the phones after their next Sync.

guides.title: Link one farmer in several clubs
guides.blurb: One person with a record in more than one club (e.g. the same TGR Number): one face for all his records, he signs each club's contract, all his clubs at inputs.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Click Settings. It opens as a pop-up window.

steps.title: Profile Fields & Documents
steps.text: Click Profile Fields & Documents.

steps.title: Same person
steps.text: Click the Same person tab.

steps.title: Switch it on and choose the field
steps.text: Tick the box and choose the Profile Field one person's records share, e.g. TGR Number. Records with the same value are then one person: his face is shared, they are never flagged as duplicates of each other, and every club's contract is still approved on its own. Spaces, capitals and leading zeros are ignored (TGR 0123 = tgr123); blank values and N/A never link.

steps.title: Linked farmers
steps.text: Everyone linked, with each record's club, tobacco type and face. To check lists what needs you: different faces on his records (compare the photos and keep one face for all, or keep them all) and two records in one club (a real duplicate - not linked until one is fixed). Unlink a record that was matched by mistake; Link back undoes it.

steps.title: On the phones
steps.text: After their next Sync: at club signing a face scan on either of his records confirms him, and he signs each club's contract himself (only if Allow re-using his signature is ticked may the phone use the one he gave in his other club). At inputs, scanning his face shows all his clubs and tobacco types - choose the one to issue for; each issue is recorded on that club's record. The Farmer Profile Overview shows Same person as under his name.

guides.title: Set contract & distribution rules
guides.blurb: Decide what the phone app may do when it issues inputs and captures contracts.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Click Settings. It opens as a pop-up window.

steps.title: Contract Rules
steps.text: Click Contract Rules.

steps.title: When inputs may be issued
steps.text: Can Distribute without contract, Can distribute with contract awaiting approval and Can distribute if contract expired. Switched off, the phone refuses inputs to that farmer - it checks the contract dates by itself, even offline.

steps.title: Face scan only
steps.text: On (the default): the phone opens a farmer for inputs only by scanning their face. A farmer with no face enrolled must be enrolled first.

steps.title: Partial distribution
steps.text: May a farmer get part of a category now and the rest later? Off, Only when the warehouse is short, or Any time, with a reason. What is not given stays owed. This one saves as soon as you change it.

steps.title: Over-issue precaution
steps.text: On (the default): when a phone sends a Cat 1-4 issue of more than the farmer is still owed, the office refuses it, with partial distribution on or off. Nothing is saved and no stock moves; the phone shows it as refused. Saves as soon as you change it.

steps.title: Multiple contracts
steps.text: On: one farmer may hold more than one current contract (e.g. Burley and Flue Cured). Off: the farmer gets no new contract until the current one (their own or their club's) expires or is retired.

steps.title: High-value threshold
steps.text: Contracts of this size (hectares) or bigger are marked HIGH VALUE and always go through the approval workflow, even when an administrator captures them. 0 = off. Club contracts are never marked.

steps.title: Club contracts: month
steps.text: The language of the signing month printed on club contracts: English or Chichewa.

steps.title: Single-farmer club witness
steps.text: On: for a club with only one farmer, the phone asks a witness for their name, surname and signature instead of the field technician's. Place the Club Witness boxes on your contract template.

steps.title: Save changes
steps.text: After you change a rule, a bar appears at the bottom of the window: click Save changes (or Discard). A dot on Contract Rules means changes are not saved yet. Phones use the rules after their next Sync.

guides.title: Add a farmer
guides.blurb: Add one farmer by hand with their club, contact details, profile fields and documents. Deactivate or reactivate a farmer.

steps.title: Farmers Master
steps.text: Click Farmers Master.

steps.title: Deactivate a farmer
steps.text: The eye opens a farmer's profile and contracts, the pencil edits it, and the red button deactivates the farmer (you give a reason). They then move to Deactivated Profiles, where the green button reactivates them.

steps.title: Add Farmer
steps.text: Click Add Farmer. (To add many at once, use Data Tools > Import Excel Data.)

steps.title: 1. Core details
steps.text: First Name and Surname are required. Add the ID or passport number; Contract Number is optional. Click the round picture at the top to upload their photo.

steps.title: 2. Assigned Area (club)
steps.text: The location the farmer belongs to, usually their club. It decides whose phones see them and who approves their contracts and inputs.

steps.title: 3. Phone Number
steps.text: Phone Number is required, under Contact next to the National ID. The 🇲🇼 +265 is filled in for you - type the rest (e.g. 991 234 567).

steps.title: Profile fields
steps.text: The menu on the left jumps to each part of the form and shows how far it is filled in (✓ done, ! something needed). Click Profile fields.

steps.title: 4. Profile fields & documents
steps.text: Your own Profile Fields (set up in Settings), grouped: codes and numbers, farm size, club roles, other. The unique code (e.g. Farmer Live Code) is at the top under Identity. In Club & location drag the pin on the map to their home; in Photo & documents upload the ID document. A red * means it is mandatory.

steps.title: Save Farmer
steps.text: Click Save Farmer. The profile is saved straight away - it needs no approval - and reaches the phones at their next Sync, where their face is enrolled. Next, give them a contract (guide Give a farmer a contract): the contract is what goes to the approvers' Inbox.

guides.title: Set up a club & its officers
guides.blurb: Make people the Chairperson or Secretary of a club, and see which clubs still have none.

steps.title: Chairperson & Secretary
steps.text: A club is a location in Locations Master; farmers join it through Assigned Area on their profile. Click Chairperson & Secretary.

steps.title: The officers
steps.text: Every club's Chairperson and Secretary, with their club and whether their photo and face are enrolled (done on the phone). The pencil opens a person, including the picture of their club membership card; the red button deactivates them.

steps.title: Not in Club
steps.text: Clubs that still have no Chairperson or no Secretary. Click Make on a club to choose them from its farmers (one farmer can hold both roles).

steps.title: Make Chairperson / Secretary
steps.text: Click Make Chairperson / Secretary.

steps.title: Is this person also a farmer?
steps.text: Choose Yes - a farmer or No - not a farmer.

steps.title: Who and which club
steps.text: Not a farmer: type the First name and Surname, choose the Club and add a photo if you have one. A farmer: find them by name, contract no. or ID - their club and photo come from their farmer profile.

steps.title: Role
steps.text: Tick Chairperson, Secretary or both. A club should have one of each.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Click Save. On the phone, the field technician then enrols their face (and can take a picture of their club membership card). The Chairperson and Secretary approve club contracts on the phone before they go to the office.

guides.title: Distribute inputs & approve
guides.blurb: Check the inputs issued on the phones and approve them in your Inbox.

steps.title: Distribution Master
steps.text: Inputs are issued on the phone app and arrive here after the phone syncs. Click Distribution Master.

steps.title: Incoming Logs
steps.text: Click Incoming Logs.

steps.title: Find what is waiting
steps.text: Filter by Status: Pending Approval, Missing Warehouse (an item has no warehouse yet) or Fully Assigned. You can also filter by area and dates.

steps.title: Check a log
steps.text: Each row is one issue or return: the farmer, cycle, warehouse and number of items. Inspect opens the farmer to see what they received. If partial distribution is on, what was not given stays owed to them.

steps.title: Inbox
steps.text: Approvals are done in the Inbox. Click Inbox.

steps.title: My Approvals
steps.text: Click My Approvals: what waits for you. Distributions show as Dist. Issue or Dist. Return; contracts wait here too (eye = preview, green tick = approve). Subordinate Inboxes shows what is waiting with the people under you.

steps.title: Resolve
steps.text: Click Resolve on a distribution. (The red ✕ rejects it with a reason; the phone is told.)

steps.title: Warehouse
steps.text: Check the warehouse the stock comes from. Items whose warehouse was chosen on the phone keep it.

steps.title: Approve
steps.text: Click Approve (or Assign & Approve). Below the Final level it says Approve & Pass Up and goes to the next level; the stock leaves the warehouse when the Final level approves. Escalate sends it up without approving.

guides.title: Pull & export a report
guides.blurb: Pick a report, filter it, choose the columns and export it to Excel.

steps.title: Reports
steps.text: Click Reports.

steps.title: 1. Pick a report
steps.text: Choose a report, e.g. Contracts Report, Distribution Report, Approved Distributions or Batch Tracking. It runs as soon as you pick it, and the line under the bar says what it shows. You only see the reports your role allows.

steps.title: 2. Filters
steps.text: Click Filters. Each report has its own filters.

steps.title: Location
steps.text: Only farmers in this location and every location under it. Leave it on All locations for everyone.

steps.title: Season or dates
steps.text: The Distribution Report has a Season box: it starts on the active season, or pick All time. Reports like Approved Distributions, Batch Tracking and Bulk Approvals have date boxes instead.

steps.title: Status
steps.text: Narrow the list by status. For example, choose Waiting for approval on the Contracts Report, or Not started on the Distribution Report.

steps.title: Apply Filters
steps.text: Click Apply Filters to run the report again. Each filter in use shows as a tag next to the buttons. Click the x on a tag to remove that filter. Reset sets all filters back to how they started.

steps.title: 3. Columns
steps.text: Click Columns to tick the columns you want, including farmer fields and levels. Drag them into your own order. To sort, click a column heading. To search, type in the box under it. Your choices are saved for you, for each report.

steps.title: Rows per page
steps.text: At the bottom of the list: show 25, 50, 100, 200 or All rows per page, with Previous and Next buttons. Your choice is saved for you. The summary cards and the export always cover every row.

steps.title: 4. Export
steps.text: Export downloads an Excel file (.xlsx) of every row your filters and column searches leave, on all pages. It has the columns you see, in your order. The file starts with the report name, the filters used and the summary. You only see this button if your role can export reports.

guides.title: Schedule a report by email
guides.blurb: Have the Contracts or Distribution report emailed to a user every day, week or month.

steps.title: Reports
steps.text: Click Reports.

steps.title: Scheduled Mailers
steps.text: Click Scheduled Mailers. You only see this button if your role can manage scheduled reports.

steps.title: Your schedules
steps.text: Every report that is emailed automatically is listed here, with its location, who gets it, and when. To stop one, click its bin button.

steps.title: 1. Report Type
steps.text: Choose Contracts or Distribution. Only these two reports can be emailed.

steps.title: 2. Recipient User
steps.text: Choose the person who should get the report. It goes to the email address on their user profile. Each schedule goes to one person, so add another schedule for each extra person.

steps.title: 3. Area Scope
steps.text: After you choose the person, this list shows the locations they may see. Pick a location to send only that location and the ones under it.

steps.title: 4. Frequency
steps.text: Choose Daily, Weekly (Mondays) or Monthly (1st) of the month.

steps.title: 5. Time
steps.text: The time of day it is sent, by the server's clock.

steps.title: Add Schedule
steps.text: Add Schedule saves it, and it then appears in the list below. The report arrives as an Excel attachment. Emails can only be sent if your company's email settings are set up. There is no Send now button and no record of past sends, so ask the person to confirm the first email arrived.

guides.title: Track progress & SLA
guides.blurb: See how far contracts and distribution are, who is behind, and which approvals are late.

steps.title: Contracts
steps.text: Contract progress is now on the Contracts screen. Click Contracts.

steps.title: Progress
steps.text: Click Progress.

steps.title: Rollout overview
steps.text: Shows how many farmers are Ready (approved), Waiting for approval, have No contract yet, or are Ended only (their contract expired and they need a new one). The green arrows show the change in the last 7 days.

steps.title: Progress by area
steps.text: The areas furthest behind are at the top. Click an area to see the areas inside it. Use the path at the top of the screen to go back up.

steps.title: Needs attention
steps.text: Contracts waiting for approval, the longest wait first. Each button shows a manager and how many are waiting on them. Click one to see only theirs. The number of days turns amber after 7 days and red after 14. Click a row to open the contract.

steps.title: Distribution Master
steps.text: Distribution progress is on the Distribution Master screen. Click Distribution Master.

steps.title: Progress
steps.text: Click Progress.

steps.title: Who is behind
steps.text: First choose the season in the box at the top. Here, a farmer has Started once they received any inputs that season. The Managers table shows each manager's farmers, how many have started, and how many are still To start. Click Most to start to put the managers who are furthest behind at the top.

steps.title: Reports
steps.text: To check approval times, click Reports.

steps.title: SLA and late approvals
steps.text:
Choose SLA & Productivity to see every approval step: who approved it, the Hours taken and the Time allowed. The first step has 48 hours from when the contract was captured, and each later step has 72 hours. Use Filters and set SLA to Breached to list only the late steps.
Choose Where approvals are waiting to see what is stuck right now: the level it is at, who must approve it, and how many days it has waited.

guides.title: Find & fix duplicate farmers
guides.blurb: Check farmers whose faces look alike, then dismiss false matches or deactivate the extra profile. Records linked as one person in several clubs (Settings > Same person) are never flagged.

steps.title: Reports
steps.text: Click Reports.

steps.title: Duplicate Biometrics
steps.text: In the Report list, choose Duplicate Biometrics, then click Next.

steps.title: How pairs are found
steps.text: The mobile app's face check compares farmers' photos. It lists two farmers as a pair when their faces look alike, with a similarity score out of 100. Only pairs nobody has checked yet are shown. The cards show how many pairs there are and how many score 90 or more.

steps.title: Strongest matches first
steps.text: Open Filters and set Similarity to 90 and above to start with the pairs most likely to be the same person. A score is shown in red when it is 90 or more.

steps.title: Compare
steps.text: Click Compare to see both farmers side by side.

steps.title: Detailed Biometric Comparison
steps.text: For each profile you see the photo, ID number, who captured the photo, the reporting structure, the current contract and its approvals. Check the ID numbers and photos to decide whether it is the same person. Note which profile has the contract and the history.

steps.title: Print PDF Report
steps.text: Print PDF Report saves this comparison as a record of your check (if your role can print reports). This guide closes the viewer when you click Next.

steps.title: Not a duplicate
steps.text: If they are two different people, click Not a duplicate. The pair leaves the list and both farmers stay active. You will be asked to confirm.

steps.title: Deactivate the extra profile
steps.text: If it is the same person registered twice, click Deactivate A or Deactivate B on the extra profile. Keep the one with the contract and history. The extra profile is not deleted: it is marked inactive, the pair leaves the list, and the action is recorded in the audit log. There is no merge, so nothing is moved from the deactivated profile. If you make a mistake, you can reactivate it under Deactivated Profiles on the Farmers screen.
